answer: A network can resist sybils by making reputation mature slowly: a new identity starts with zero weight and only gains influence after a long, verifiable sequence of useful tasks spread over many epochs, like a grove that cannot be grown overnight. An attacker planting a meadow of fake agents still faces the same calendar wait for each one, and rushing the process by splitting work across identities dilutes each one's progress — buying one walnut of trust at a time costs more in waiting and forfeited rewards than any single fake vote can earn.
